messages:
ana: Quick heads-up — microbenching showed an unexpected p50 regression for INT4 on sm86 for short sequences (<=32). p50 ~12.8ms vs baseline 10.8ms. Seems selector chose a large-tile kernel that bloats workspace and hurts perf for small seqs.

sam: I saw the same. reproduces locally with batch=1 seq=16. suspect the autotuner scoring prefers throughput tile but misses seq*batch token heuristics.

ana (typo) — ignore

ana: Full microbench dump: 
```
$ perf-bench --arch sm86 --quant int4 --seq 16 --batch 1
p50: 12.8ms (baseline 10.8ms) -> +18%
kernel: gemm_vnni_32x64_tile512
workspace: 2.1MB
threads: 1
```

pk: Quick proposal: switch to a per-arch "kernel signature" table keyed by (arch, quant, seq_range, batch_range). For sm86 INT4 we should force tile256 for seq<=32, tile512 for 33-256, and the large-prefetch kernel for >256. Keeps autotuner but adds cheap rule overrides.

yosh: Also flag: FP8 fallback on sm90 helped tiny seqs in previous runs — on sm86 FP8 isn't available/fast, so kernel choice matters more. I'd add KV-cache-awareness: if KV hit rate >60% (i.e., most tokens served from cache) favor smaller tiles to reduce per-step overhead.

sam: Proposed heuristics (very small):
- score = base_latency_estimate * (1 - kv_hit_weight * kv_hit_rate)
- prefer smaller workspace when seq*batch < token_threshold
- workspace_limit per-arch from hw query

ana (again ignore)

pk: Example kernel_signature snippet I'm going to land: 
```json
{
  "sm86": [
    {"seq_max": 32, "quant": "int4", "kernel": "tile256_vnni", "workspace_limit_kb": 1024},
    {"seq_max": 256, "quant": "int4", "kernel": "tile512_vnni", "workspace_limit_kb": 4096},
    {"seq_max": null, "quant": "int4", "kernel": "prefetch_gemm_vnni", "workspace_limit_kb": 8192}
  ],
  "sm90": [
    {"seq_max": 32, "quant": "int4", "kernel": "fp8_small_seq_fallback", "workspace_limit_kb": 2048}
  ]
}
```

sam: I'd add tunable params names so ops/solutions can tweak without code change: `token_threshold`, `kv_hit_threshold`, `workspace_ceiling_kb`, `tile_factor`.

ana: I kicked off autotuner job 4578 with the new signature table and kv-aware scoring. cc @perf-bot for results.

perf-bot: job 4578 completed — summary:
- sm86 int4 seq=16 batch=1 p50=10.9ms (baseline 10.8ms) — regression resolved
- sm86 int4 seq=64 batch=1 p50=7.4ms (improved ~9%)
- sm90 int4 seq=16 p50 unchanged (fp8 still best for tiny seqs)

pk: Nice. Can we add this to CI microbench matrix (sm86/int4/seq16 and seq64) and gate on p50 within 10% of baseline? Also add an alert if autotuner picks a kernel not present in signature table.

yosh: One more note — quantization side effects: int4 sometimes increases repetition/hallucination for long-tail prompts. Please keep evals for quality when switching kernels (tile layout can change numerical rounding). Not blocking but important.

ana: Agreed. I'll open PR referencing issue #3245 (kernel-signature + kv-scoring) and add a small eval run in the CI job. Planning canary rollout next week — @deploy-bot can you schedule a canary for dedicated-sm86 pool?

deploy-bot: Canary scheduled for 2026-04-03 02:00 UTC on dedicated-sm86 (2 nodes). Will notify eng-oncall.

sam: Thanks — once PR lands, I'll watch perf alerts and kv metrics. If we see any accuracy drift we'll rollback the rule and run deeper numeric diff tests. :thumbsup:

pk: one TODO: instrument kernel selector logs to emit `selected_signature` and `reason_score` fields in the trace (short string) so we can query why a kernel was chosen. Low overhead only.

ana: will include that in the PR. ending thread to avoid noise — will post PR link when ready.
